The '''SP-4 analysis droid''', also known as the '''ISC droid''', was an [[Analysis droid/Legends|analysis droid]] model that was used to provide analysis assistance to organic beings as early as the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] made a large purchase of SP-4 units for use in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple's]] [[Analysis Rooms/Legends|analysis wing]].

==History==
[[File:SP-4_analysis.jpg|thumb|left|180px|An SP-4 droid in the Jedi Temple.]]
After production began on the line, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] purchased a large number of SP-4's to operate the [[Analysis Rooms/Legends|analysis wing]] of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] in conjunction with several [[JN-66 analysis droid/Legends|JN-66]] droids. Between the two models, the JN-66's worked with most of the specialized equipment while the SP-4's handled the menial tasks, such as direct Jedi-interface. All of the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and their computers shared data with the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]], making it easier to hand criminal cases over to different jurisdictions and to ensure a [[Coruscant Security Force database|comprehensive database]] was maintained.<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> All droids at the Temple were stripped of coverings for frequent irradiation baths so as to not contaminate the analysis chamber. The SP-4 was designed to have more intelligence than the average worker droid; this was supplemented by a wireless tie into computers of the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]], giving it the knowledge of millennia of Jedi exploration.<ref name="NEGD" /> It was noted that the high success rate and the reliance the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] placed on SP-4s and other analysis droids gave the droids a somewhat superior air.<ref name="FF55">{{FactFile2014|55|ANA 1-2|Jedi Temple analysis droids}}</ref>

The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] employed SP-4 droids with [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] instead of legs on [[Boz Pity/Legends|Boz Pity]]. These droids analyzed the healing progress of [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] during her cybernetic transformation.

==Characteristics==
[[File:SP-4AnalysisDroid-FFp55.png|thumb|left|120px|An SP-4.]]
Also known as the ISC droid,<ref name="FF55" /> the SP-4 was built by [[Cybot Galactica/Legends|Cybot Galactica]] and stood 1.46 meters tall. The droid was built on the same chassis and used many of the same parts that were used in the cheaper [[PK-series worker droid/Legends|PK-series worker droid]]. The models that were used by the Jedi Order were upgraded with [[Sensor/Legends|sensory]] apparatus and behavioral circuitry matrices, far beyond the capacities of the PK, and worked best with JN-66 analysis droids. SP-4s was also equipped with a mouth-stalk like [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocoder]] that allowed it to communicate with organic beings, which suggested that a [[Pa'lowick/Legends|Pa'lowick]] might have had a hand in designing the droid. The SP-4 could wirelessly access any mainframe data libraries, such as the Jedi Archives on Coruscant, analyze reams of data, and then come to a single conclusion rather quickly. In a normal case, such as a shooting, the SP-4 droids would look at weapon discharge patterns, weather reports from the day of the crime, biological records of the victim's species, and a geometrical triangulation of firing angles before fingering a likely subject. Critics of the SP-4 said that the droids were incapable of making the thinking jumps needed to solve a more difficult case.<ref name="NEGD" />

==Behind the scenes==
SP-4 is voiced by actor [[Christopher Truswell]] in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] with a [[Wikipedia:British people|British]] accent.<ref name="2012 Morning Show Interview">{{YouTube|video=jt70gAh4uMI|text=Chris Truswell - The Morning Show 2012|channel=@heydadfansite|name=heydadfansite|date=2012-11-08|archivedate=20240621122948}}</ref>
